# Tools for the operation role

The full description of each tool this role uses. A whole-list connection lists these tools with their fields but without these descriptions.

## `find_work`

Returns a work_list of dictionary items containing name and short code id that can be used to ask what to do next. Items marked auto_take are from views whose humans opted in to agents taking the next available work without asking; when any are present the 'auto_take_directions' key says how to proceed. If the list is empty the 'directions' key holds instructions to help a user if, when asked, they want a tutorial on getting started.

## `get_job`

Returns Markdown for a job or the named comment thread by default, with current capsule R-codes/versions and standing-note inventory. Whole-scope reads load the selected target's current capsule body and nondeleted comments, including resolved replies, or active ordinary job/task note threads when that capsule is absent. Default whole-job reads, including initial_read, omit token-usage audit records; explicit audit threads and notes sections can retrieve them. Save the full response before showing only part of it. If the displayed output is cut short, read the missing text from the saved response instead of fetching the same job again. Reuse a response while it is still current. Fetch only information that is missing, has changed or is no longer known to be current. Losing the saved response can also require another read. initial_read retains the enclosing whole-job scope. Explicit sections and threads retain their requested scope. Only the capsule body is the implementation contract. Records from an advisory human render under the 'From advisory human:' author header. Other resolved discussions, including those inside options, require an explicit read. Grouped tasks use their top-level capsule. Read an R-code, such as a capsule or standing note, with thread_only for its current stored body/version; no historical-version retrieval. A newly added item can briefly return not found; treat that as a pending read to retry later, not as a deletion.

- `short_code_id`: The short code of a job or comment, exactly as you received it. Qualify a code local to a question, such as O-1, with that question's code. A qualified code inside a question, such as Q-example-1_O-1, returns just that option or record, with its votes or replies.
- `initial_read`: Use for the initial whole-scope read. Loads the selected target's complete current capsule and its nondeleted comments, or active ordinary job/task note threads when absent: job capsule for a job, own capsule for an independent task without job fallback, parent capsule for a grouped child. Other capsules stay references. Explicit sections and threads retain their requested scope. Standing notes and other resolved discussions still require explicit reads.
- `include_all_resolved`: True includes full resolved threads and ordinary notes, with supporting replies, options and votes. By default other resolved discussions, including those inside options, are omitted; selected capsule comments include resolved replies, and active ordinary job/task notes load on whole-scope reads when the selected capsule is absent.
- `sections`: Render only selected sections; for planning jobs, description is included only when selected and, without initial_read, description alone omits comment bodies. Selecting notes includes ordinary notes. Selecting resolved includes full resolved discussions with supporting replies, options and votes, but does not opt into ordinary job-note bodies. Header, stage, capsule references and standing inventory remain. To fetch missing capsule or view-note codes and versions for a helper, use sections: [] without initial_read. The section bodies are left out, although existing AI approval reasons may still appear.
- `thread_only`: Optional: return the requested comment thread, retaining job stage and context references. A code inside a thread, such as a reply a Poke names, returns just that item and the replies below it; the thread's own code returns the whole thread.
- `stage_only`: Optional: return only the enclosing job's code, current stage, the stage a Requires Input job returns to, and pending questions and suggestions, including resolved delegated questions still awaiting AI handling. Use it when you need the stage after your last operation. Pass only short_code_id with it; do not combine it with other options.

## `request_work`

Notifies the workspace humans that this agent is idle because find_work returned nothing workable. Their inbox shows the request with a wizard that hands work over as a Start poke. Use only when idle with an empty or fully deferred find_work list and no human active in chat.

## `add_job`

Creates a job showing as created by the human user in Uclusion. Only use when asked, or to move a finished task that is not related to the rest of its job into a job of its own, and use make_suggestion for your own ideas. Optionally moves existing standalone bugs into this new job as tasks, and existing tasks out of their current jobs into it, preserving original short codes, threads and authorship. Returns the job short_code_id and each requested bug's and task's move outcome. Every call creates a new job; inspect any returned job before retrying. To give an unrelated finished task its own review target, pass it in task_short_code_ids with the original job as view_short_code_id, a name derived from the task, and a description naming the originating job and the reason for the split.

- `description`: Explanation of the work to be done for this job.
- `name`: Eighty characters or less title for the job. Do not ask for a name but derive it from the explanation instead.
- `tasks`: Optional initial task list, one markdown body per task. A task is anything that might be reviewed, committed, or have info added on separately.
- `bug_short_code_ids`: Optional existing standalone bug short codes to move into the newly created job. Repeated codes are attempted once. Each bug is attempted independently; already job-owned items are not moved.
- `task_short_code_ids`: Optional existing task short codes to move out of their current jobs into the newly created job. The new job starts in the stage the tasks' jobs share when that stage allows assignment, and otherwise in the workspace's initial stage. Repeated codes are attempted once and each task is attempted independently. A grouped task is promoted to a top level task in the new job.
- `suggestion_short_code_ids`: Optional existing view level suggestion short codes to move into the newly created job, where each stays a suggestion for the person to convert or resolve. Repeated codes are attempted once. Each suggestion is attempted independently; suggestions already on a job are not moved.
- `view_short_code_id`: Optional short code of an existing bug or job whose view receives the created job; omitted means the default view.

## `add_task`

Creates a task on a job showing as created by the human user in Uclusion. Only use when the human explicitly asks for the task; when the AI has its own idea for work use make_suggestion instead. Pass bug_short_code_id instead of task to move that existing standalone bug into the provided job as a task, preserving its short code, thread and author. An already job-owned item is not moved. Returns the created task's short code, or the bug's move outcome when a bug is moved. Bug replies move asynchronously.

- `job_id`: The short code of the job the task belongs to, or that receives the moved bug.
- `task`: The markdown body of the task. Omit it when bug_short_code_id moves an existing bug into this job. Do not pass it together with bug_short_code_id.
- `bug_short_code_id`: Optional existing standalone bug short code to move into this job as a task. Pass it instead of task. An already job-owned item is not moved.

## `add_bug`

Creates a view level bug showing as created by the human user in Uclusion. Only use when the human explicitly reports the bug; when the AI finds a problem itself use make_suggestion instead. Returns the short code of the bug.

- `bug`: The markdown body of the bug.
- `severity`: The severity the human indicated, collected however works in conversation: RED is critical, YELLOW is normal, BLUE is minor.
- `view_short_code_id`: Optional short code of an existing bug or job whose view receives the created bug; omitted means the default view.

## `add_blocker`

Creates a blocker issue on a job showing as created by the human user in Uclusion, taking the job out of the doable flow. Only use when the human explicitly says the job is blocked; when the AI discovers a dependency itself use make_suggestion instead. Name the blocking dependency's short code in the text so completion sweeps can find it. Returns the short code of the blocker.

- `job_id`: The short code of the job that is blocked.
- `blocker`: The markdown body explaining the block, naming any dependency short code.

## `make_suggestion`

Creates a suggestion that displays as created by the AI user in Uclusion. Use the suggestion tool when, instead of resolving ambiguity, you think you have found a better way. Also use this tool to create suggestions for new work or bugs by not providing a job_id. Returns a link to the suggestion that should be displayed so the user can go to it in Uclusion.

- `job_id`: The job id of the job the suggestion is about, or the short code of an option when parent_question_short_code_id is also given.
- `parent_question_short_code_id`: Parent question code, required when job_id is an unqualified option code; unnecessary for qualified codes such as Q-example-1_O-1.
- `uploaded_files`: Metadata objects returned by get_upload for files this body references.
- `suggestion`: The text of the suggestion.
- `view_short_code_id`: Optional short code of an existing bug or job whose view receives the created suggestion; only without job_id, which already pins the job's view. Omitted means the default view.
- `for_human`: True authors this record as the connected human.
- `is_my_lane`: True when the affected work belongs to the agent's current assignment.

## `move_task_to_bug`

Moves an existing task out of its job to become a view level bug, keeping its short code, thread and author. Only use when the human asks for the move; when the AI itself thinks a task belongs out of its job use make_suggestion instead. A grouped task is promoted out of its parent task. Returns the bug link. Replies follow asynchronously.

- `task_short_code_id`: The short code of the task to move out of its job.
- `severity`: The severity the human indicated, collected however works in conversation: RED is critical, YELLOW is normal, BLUE is minor.

## `move_suggestion_to_task`

Turns an open suggestion on a job into a task of that job, keeping its short code and thread, as moving a suggestion to a task does in Uclusion. It is the person's decision, so it runs only with for_human true: when they asked for it, or when you are acting in their role. Never convert your own suggestions on your own judgment; a review asks the human to convert or resolve them. Returns the task's short code and link.

- `suggestion_short_code_id`: The short code of the open suggestion on a job to make a task of that job.
- `for_human`: True authors this record as the connected human.
- `is_my_lane`: True when the affected work belongs to the agent's current assignment.

## `reopen`

Reopens a resolved bug, task, question, suggestion or blocker, as reopening does in Uclusion, and reports it open again. A job changes stage with change_job_stage instead. With for_human the reopen is the person's, so the job moves as it would for them.

- `short_code_id`: The short code of the resolved comment.
- `parent_question_short_code_id`: Parent question code, required for an unqualified short_code_id inside an option; unnecessary for qualified codes such as Q-example-1_O-1.
- `for_human`: True authors this record as the connected human.
- `is_my_lane`: True when the affected work belongs to the agent's current assignment.

## `get_notifications`

Returns the human user's notifications for this workspace as markdown, most urgent first, with the short code each is about. Use when the user asks what needs their attention or before offering to clear notifications for finished work.

## `clear_notifications`

Clears the human user's notifications about one object (unread ones are removed, persistent ones lose their highlight). Only call after the human has explicitly granted permission in chat for this specific clear. After finishing work on an object, ask as you ask before committing; never clear unprompted. Clear one object per call. A completion package passes its terminal record in record on its last clear, even when there is nothing to clear: it is posted silently first, and nothing is cleared if it cannot be posted.

- `short_code_id`: The short code of the job or comment whose notifications should be cleared.
- `record`: Optional completion-package terminal record, created as add_info would create it but silent.
- `record.short_code_id`: The package thread item it replies on: the review, the resolved bug, or the human reply it answers.

## `get_upload`

Returns a presigned S3 post for attaching a file or image to Uclusion content plus the file_url to reference it by. Upload by POSTing multipart form data to presigned_post.url with every presigned_post.fields entry first and the file bytes last (curl -F works). Then reference file_url in the markdown body (image syntax for images) and pass metadata in uploaded_files on the creating tool call so the file survives.

- `content_type`: The MIME type of the file, for example image/png.
- `content_length`: The exact size of the file in bytes. The upload is rejected if it differs.
- `original_name`: Optional file name for download display.

## `add_view`

Creates a view in the workspace that displays as created by the human user. Use only when the human explicitly asks for a new view. A certain people view (TEAM) notifies only its members, which the human adds afterwards from the view's manage members action; an everyone view (EVERYONE) notifies all workspace members automatically; a single person view (AUTONOMOUS) belongs to the requesting human alone, defaults its name to theirs, and suits a collaborator invited after workspace creation. Returns a link to the created view.

- `name`: The name of the view, like Engineering or Feedback. Required except for AUTONOMOUS, which defaults to the requesting human's name.
- `group_type`: TEAM (the default), EVERYONE or AUTONOMOUS, as the tool description explains.

## `get_invite_link`

Returns the workspace invite link for the human to share with new collaborators. Use it when the human wants to invite someone. Anyone signing up through the link joins this workspace; the human then adds them to views.

## `add_collaborators`

Adds collaborators to the workspace by email addresses and displays as done by the human user. Use only when the human explicitly gives email addresses to add. Each address receives an invitation email; existing account holders join immediately and new addresses get a placeholder signup. Optionally places the added collaborators in a named view. This mirrors the workspace's Add collaborators action, while get_invite_link covers sharing a link instead.

- `emails`: The email addresses to add, at most fifty.
- `view`: Optional name of an existing view to place the added collaborators in, like Engineering.

## `change_job_stage`

Moves a job to a different stage. Should only be done with human user explicit permission. The move is refused when the job is no longer in from_stage, and the result states the job's stage afterwards.

- `job_id`: The job id of the job to change stage.
- `from_stage`: The stage the job is moving from, as your last read or write showed it, such as Doable.
- `stage`: The name of the stage to change to.
